trials.title: The LYMPH Trial — microsurgical versus conservative treatment of chronic breast-cancer-associated lymphoedema
trials.population: Adults with chronic breast-cancer-associated upper-limb lymphoedema
trials.design: Pragmatic randomised international multicentre comparison of microsurgery and conservative complex decongestive therapy
trials.caution: Recruitment and registration do not show that surgery is better. The primary completion date is still in the future and no results are reported here.

trials.title: Efficacy of GLP-1 receptor agonists in upper- and lower-extremity lymphoedema
trials.population: Adults with unilateral upper- or lower-extremity lymphoedema who meet the study criteria
trials.design: Early Phase 1, open-label, single-group interventional study
trials.caution: This is an early, uncontrolled study with no posted results. It does not establish GLP-1 medicines as a lymphoedema treatment and is not a recommendation to use them.

title: Lymphoedema research: what works and what is still uncertain
summary: A research-based guide to established care, promising options, unanswered questions, and the evidence behind each conclusion.
changes: Replaced the generic introduction with three evidence-status takeaways, each linked directly to its supporting references.
Reorganised reviewed findings around treatment and management, medicines, children and adolescents, and understanding and diagnosis.
Clearly labels the English synthesis as source-reviewed but not clinician-reviewed, and the Chinese version as AI-assisted and not independently language-reviewed.

items.title: Current care has established foundations
items.summary: Current guidance supports individually assessed compression, skin care, movement and exercise, and appropriate decongestive therapy as foundations of lymphoedema management.

sources.label: Healthdirect Australia — How is lymphoedema treated?
NHS — Treatment for lymphoedema
International Society of Lymphology 2023 consensus — conservative treatment

items.title: Newer options may help selected people
items.summary: Newer compression delivery, progressive resistance training, and specialist microsurgery may help particular populations, but the findings do not make any one option suitable for everyone.

items.title: Evidence strength changes what we can conclude
items.summary: A small study, a randomised trial, a systematic review, and a registered trial with no results support different levels of confidence; registration alone does not show that a treatment works.

treatmentManagement.intro: Established care is individualised. Current guidance describes compression, skin care, exercise and movement, and decongestive therapy as core approaches; specialist procedures may be considered for selected people.

sources.label: Healthdirect Australia — lymphoedema treatment
NHS — lymphoedema treatment
International Society of Lymphology consensus — conservative treatment
International Society of Lymphology consensus — operative treatment

medicines.intro: No medicine is established as routine treatment for uncomplicated peripheral lymphoedema itself. Antibiotics are used for diagnosed infections such as cellulitis, not as general lymphoedema treatment; long-term diuretics are generally discouraged except for selected coexisting conditions or complications. A registered GLP-1 study has no posted results and is not a treatment recommendation.
